## Citation and licensed use

**Scoped note:** C. G. Jung, *Psychologische Typen* (Zürich: Rascher & Cie., 1921), introduction, 7–13, consulted in Project Gutenberg ebook 61543, accessed September 8, 2026.

The [Jung–Pauli dossier](../../../../dossiers/jung-pauli-psychoid.md#four-functions-two-attitudes-native-senarius) **compares** Jung’s distinction between attitude and function with the native account of explicit and implicate offices. This source **sources** the historical typological distinction and **qualifies** its cross-register use. Jung’s two attitudes are not two additional functions. The comparison does not derive Taylor’s native 4+2, eight determinations or X/x, establish a psychophysical ontology, or claim independent empirical validation of Jung’s typology. The dossier retains those separate argument and research standings.

## Passages and excerpts

<a id="jung-1921-psychologische-typen-p001"></a>
### jung-1921-psychologische-typen-p001 — Attitudes and relative predominance

**Paraphrase:** Jung distinguishes interest directed toward the object from interest directed toward the subject and its own psychic processes. Both mechanisms occur in each person. A type describes relative habitual predominance; the other mechanism is not extinguished. His account also describes compensation and the difficulty of judging one’s own type.

**Locator:** Introduction, printed pp. 7–12; both mechanisms at p. 8, directional contrast at pp. 9–10, relative predominance at pp. 11–12.

**Provenance:** Project Gutenberg ebook 61543, German transcription of Rascher, Zürich, 1921; saved HTML declared above, introduction anchor `Einleitung` and printed page markers. Complete introduction read 2026-09-08; contextual paraphrase checked against that text.

**Source relation:** Paraphrased.

**Status:** paraphrase-ready; no quotation admitted.

**Use boundary:** Reports Jung’s account of attitudes and predominance, not a demonstrated psychological law or two extra functions. The dossier’s native threshold comparison remains a distinct operation.

**Consumer:** The [Jung–Pauli dossier](../../../../dossiers/jung-pauli-psychoid.md#four-functions-two-attitudes-native-senarius) **compares** oriented reception with the native opening and return.

<a id="jung-1921-psychologische-typen-p002"></a>
### jung-1921-psychologische-typen-p002 — Four functions and a corrected classification

**Paraphrase:** Jung separately identifies thinking, feeling, sensation and intuition as basic functions. A function’s habitual predominance gives a corresponding type, each of which can be introverted or extraverted. He withdraws his earlier identification of the thinking type with introversion and the feeling type with extraversion, because closer investigation made that conflation untenable.

**Locator:** Introduction, printed pp. 12–13, closing discussion of basic functions and correction of the two preliminary accounts.

**Provenance:** Project Gutenberg ebook 61543, German transcription of Rascher, Zürich, 1921; saved HTML declared above, introduction anchor `Einleitung`, page markers 12 and 13. Complete introduction read 2026-09-08; contextual paraphrase checked against the concluding paragraphs.

**Source relation:** Paraphrased.

**Status:** paraphrase-ready; no quotation admitted.

**Use boundary:** Distinguishes function from attitude within this 1921 introduction. Four functions oriented in two ways do not derive six QL positions or Taylor’s eight determinations. No CW6 acquisition is needed for this admitted German passage; no CW6 equivalence is asserted.

**Consumer:** The [Jung–Pauli dossier](../../../../dossiers/jung-pauli-psychoid.md#four-functions-two-attitudes-native-senarius) **returns-to** its A18/M33 comparison with the two classifications distinguished.
